nodes.title: Origin and Evolution of Universe
prelimsNote: Big Bang ~13.8 billion years ago: expansion from a singularity; evidence — red shift of galaxies (Hubble's law) and cosmic microwave background radiation.
Expanding universe supported by red shift (Doppler effect) — UPSC 2012 asked for evidence of expansion.
Stages: inflation → formation of hydrogen/helium → stars and galaxies → heavier elements made in stars (nucleosynthesis).
Elements essential for life (C, H, O, N) were formed in stars; UPSC 2012 tested which elements are crucial for life.

nodes.title: Origin of Universe
prelimsNote: Steady State theory (Hoyle, Bondi, Gold): universe has no beginning, matter continuously created — rejected after CMB discovery (1965).
Big Bang is the accepted model; light-year is a unit of distance (~9.46 trillion km) — UPSC 2021.
Galaxies → Milky Way (spiral) → Solar System in the Orion arm; nearest star after the Sun is Proxima Centauri.
Dark matter and dark energy make up most of the universe's mass–energy (~95%).

nodes.title: Big Bang theory
prelimsNote: Proposed by Georges Lemaître (1927); 'Big Bang' term coined by Fred Hoyle; supported by Hubble's 1929 observation of receding galaxies.
Cosmic Microwave Background (Penzias & Wilson, 1965) is relic radiation from the early universe.
Universe is still expanding and the expansion is accelerating (dark energy).
Trap: Big Bang was not an explosion in space — it is the expansion of space itself.

nodes.title: Theories of Origin
prelimsNote: Nebular hypothesis (Kant, Laplace): Sun and planets formed from a rotating gas cloud.
Planetesimal hypothesis (Chamberlin & Moulton) and Tidal hypothesis (Jeans & Jeffreys) — older dualistic theories.
Modern view: solar nebula collapsed ~4.6 billion years ago; planets formed by accretion.
Inner planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars) are rocky/terrestrial; outer are gas/ice giants; Venus and Uranus rotate in the retrograde direction.

nodes.title: Origin and Evolution of Earth
prelimsNote: Earth formed ~4.54 billion years ago; differentiation produced core, mantle and crust.
Atmosphere evolved in three stages: primordial gases lost → degassing from interior → oxygen added by photosynthesis.
Oceans formed from condensed water vapour released by volcanic degassing.
Earth's magnetic field (from the liquid outer core) has reversed many times — recorded in rocks (UPSC 2018).

nodes.title: Geological TIme Scale
prelimsNote: Eons → Eras → Periods → Epochs; Precambrian covers ~88% of Earth's history.
Palaeozoic (age of invertebrates/fishes), Mesozoic (age of reptiles/dinosaurs, ended ~66 mya), Cenozoic (age of mammals).
Himalayan uplift began in the Cenozoic (Tertiary); Aravallis are among the oldest fold mountains (Precambrian).
Holocene epoch began ~11,700 years ago; 'Anthropocene' was proposed but rejected as a formal epoch in 2024.

nodes.title: Internal Structure of Earth & Plate Tectonics
prelimsNote: Layers: crust (Moho discontinuity) → mantle (asthenosphere is the weak, partly molten upper mantle) → outer core (liquid) → inner core (solid).
Seismic waves: P-waves are primary, longitudinal, travel through solids and liquids, recorded first; S-waves are transverse and cannot pass through liquid (UPSC 2023).
S-wave shadow zone beyond 103° shows the outer core is liquid; P-wave shadow zone 103°–142°.
Plate boundaries: convergent (Himalaya, trenches), divergent (mid-ocean ridges, rift valleys), transform (San Andreas).
Earth's internal heat comes from radioactive decay and primordial heat (UPSC 2013).

nodes.title: Continental Drift Theory — Evidence & Implications
prelimsNote: Alfred Wegener (1912): Pangaea surrounded by Panthalassa; split into Laurasia and Gondwanaland.
Evidence: jigsaw fit of coasts, matching fossils (Mesosaurus, Glossopteris), tillite deposits, placer gold in Ghana from Brazil.
Weakness: no convincing driving force — later explained by sea-floor spreading (Hess, 1960s) and plate tectonics.
Palaeomagnetism and sea-floor striping support drift; UPSC 2014 linked drift with biological evolution.

nodes.title: Earthquakes — Causes, Types & Disaster Management
prelimsNote: Focus (hypocentre) vs epicentre; magnitude (Richter, logarithmic) vs intensity (Modified Mercalli).
Most earthquakes occur along plate boundaries — ~80% in the Pacific Ring of Fire.
India's seismic zones: II to V; Zone V includes NE India, J&K, Himachal, Uttarakhand, Kutch, Andaman & Nicobar.
NDMA (Disaster Management Act 2005) chaired by the PM; NDRF for response.

nodes.title: Volcanoes & Volcanic Activity
prelimsNote: Types: shield (basaltic, gentle — Hawaii), composite/strato (explosive — Fuji, Vesuvius), caldera; Deccan Traps are fissure flood basalts.
Intrusive landforms: batholith, laccolith, lopolith, sill (horizontal), dyke (vertical).
Barren Island (Andaman) is India's only active volcano (UPSC 2018); Narcondam is dormant.
Pacific Ring of Fire hosts most active volcanoes.

nodes.title: Tsunamis — Causes & Preparedness
prelimsNote: Caused mainly by undersea earthquakes (thrust faulting), also landslides and volcanic eruptions.
Low amplitude in deep ocean, rises sharply near coasts (shoaling).
2004 Indian Ocean tsunami (Sumatra, M9.1) led to the Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre at INCOIS, Hyderabad (2007).
Mangroves reduce tsunami damage (UPSC 2011).

nodes.title: Mountain Building — Types of Mountains & Formation
prelimsNote: Fold mountains (Himalaya, Alps, Andes, Rockies) at convergent boundaries; block mountains/horsts (Vosges, Black Forest) with rift valleys/grabens.
Volcanic mountains (Kilimanjaro, Fuji); residual mountains (Aravallis, Eastern Ghats).
Syntaxial bends at the ends of the Himalaya (Nanga Parbat in the west, Namcha Barwa in the east) — UPSC 2011.
Himalaya is young, still rising; Aravallis are among the oldest fold mountains.

nodes.title: Plains & Plateaus — Formation & Significance
prelimsNote: Plains: alluvial/depositional (Indo-Gangetic), erosional (peneplains), structural.
Plateaus: Deccan (lava), Tibetan (highest), Chota Nagpur (mineral-rich), Malwa.
Rann of Kutch formed from repeated sea-level falls — marshland (UPSC 2023).
Karewas (Kashmir) are lacustrine deposits suited to saffron.

nodes.title: Indian Monsoon and Local Phenomenon
prelimsNote: Monsoon onset linked to ITCZ shift north, Tibetan plateau heating, tropical easterly jet and shift of subtropical westerly jet.
Monsoon = seasonal reversal of winds (UPSC 2012); SW monsoon arrives in Kerala around 1 June; NE monsoon gives Tamil Nadu winter rain.
Local storms: Kalbaisakhi/Nor'westers (WB, Odisha), Mango showers (Kerala–Karnataka), Blossom showers (coffee), Loo (N India).
Western disturbances bring winter rain/snow to NW India — beneficial for rabi wheat.
El Niño weakens and positive IOD strengthens the monsoon (UPSC 2011, 2017).

nodes.title: Earth Atmosphere: structure and components
prelimsNote: Nitrogen ~78%, oxygen ~21%, argon ~0.93%, CO₂ ~0.04%; water vapour and dust vary.

Layers: troposphere (weather, ~8 km at poles to ~18 km at equator) → stratosphere (ozone, ideal for jet flights — UPSC 2011) → mesosphere (coldest, meteors burn) → thermosphere/ionosphere → exosphere.
Ionosphere reflects radio waves, enabling long-distance radio communication (UPSC 2011).
Temperature falls ~6.5 °C per km in the troposphere (normal lapse rate).

nodes.title: Insolation
prelimsNote: Insolation depends on angle of sun's rays, length of day, transparency of atmosphere and land configuration.

Infrared waves are largely absorbed by water vapour concentrated in the lower atmosphere (UPSC 2023); the equator receives far less than '10 times' the poles' insolation — UPSC 2023's claim was false.
Heat budget: about 35 units reflected (albedo) of 100 received; the atmosphere is heated mainly from below by terrestrial radiation.
Maximum insolation is over subtropical deserts (clear skies), not at the equator.

nodes.title: Temperature
prelimsNote: Temperature inversion: warmer air above colder air — long winter nights, calm air, clear sky, snow cover (UPSC 2012).
Continentality: land heats and cools faster than water because water's specific heat is higher — UPSC 2023 tested this as a Statement-I/II pair.
Isotherms bend equatorward over continents in winter and poleward in summer.
Dew forms on clear calm nights; cloudy nights prevent dew because clouds radiate heat back (UPSC 2019).

nodes.title: Atmospheric Pressure and Pressure Belts
prelimsNote: Pressure belts: Equatorial Low (doldrums), Subtropical Highs (~30°, horse latitudes), Subpolar Lows (~60°), Polar Highs.
Subtropical highs from descending air create hot deserts on western margins of continents (UPSC 2011).
Belts shift north–south with the apparent movement of the Sun.
Pressure decreases with height; isobars join equal-pressure points.

nodes.title: Wind Systems (Planetary, Secondary, and Local winds)
prelimsNote: Planetary winds: trade winds (easterlies), westerlies, polar easterlies; deflected by Coriolis force (right in NH, left in SH).
Southern Hemisphere westerlies are stronger and persistent — 'Roaring Forties, Furious Fifties' — due to less land (UPSC 2011).
Jet streams: high-altitude westerly winds; the subtropical westerly jet's northward shift aids the Indian monsoon's onset.
Local winds: Loo (hot, N India), Chinook/Foehn (warm, dry descending — 'snow eater'), Sirocco, Mistral (cold, Rhône valley), Harmattan ('doctor', West Africa), Bora (cold, Adriatic).

nodes.title: Humidity and Condensation (Evaporation, cloud formation, fog)
prelimsNote: Absolute humidity = water vapour per unit volume; relative humidity = actual ÷ capacity at that temperature (%).
Dew point: temperature at which air becomes saturated.
Condensation forms: dew, frost, fog, mist, clouds (cirrus — high/wispy, cumulus — fluffy, stratus — layered, nimbus — rain).
Thunder is caused by rapid heating and expansion of air from lightning (UPSC 2013).

nodes.title: Precipitation (Types of rainfall, world distribution)
prelimsNote: Convectional (equatorial, afternoon), orographic (windward vs rain-shadow leeward), cyclonic/frontal.
Rain-shadow examples: Deccan plateau east of the Western Ghats, Leh.
Highest rainfall: Mawsynram–Cherrapunji (Meghalaya); lowest in India: Ladakh, western Rajasthan.
Equatorial regions get rain throughout the year (UPSC 2015).

nodes.title: Air Masses, Fronts, and Cyclones (Tropical and Temperate)
prelimsNote: Tropical cyclones need warm sea surface (>27 °C), Coriolis force (none within ~5° of the equator), low wind shear, pre-existing disturbance.
No tropical cyclones in the South Atlantic and south-east Pacific due to cold currents and wind shear (UPSC 2015).
Temperate (extra-tropical) cyclones form along fronts between air masses; move west to east in the westerlies.
Names: hurricanes (Atlantic, NE Pacific), typhoons (NW Pacific), cyclones (Indian Ocean), willy-willies (Australia).

nodes.title: Climate Classification (Köppen's scheme)
prelimsNote: Based on temperature and precipitation tied to vegetation: A (tropical humid), B (dry), C (warm temperate), D (cold), E (polar), H (highland).
India: Amw (Malabar/Konkan coast), As (Coromandel coast), Aw (tropical savannah — most of peninsula), BWhw (western Rajasthan), Cwg (Ganga plains), Dfc (Arunachal), E (Kashmir highlands).
Savannah: grasses with scattered trees, distinct wet and dry seasons (UPSC 2012, 2021); Mediterranean: winter rain, summer drought.
Steppe: temperate grasslands of Eurasia (UPSC 2013).

nodes.title: Ocean Currents and their climatic influence (El Niño and La Niña)
prelimsNote: El Niño: warm water off Peru, weak trade winds, usually weak Indian monsoon; La Niña: the reverse (UPSC 2011).
ENSO = El Niño + Southern Oscillation (pressure see-saw between Tahiti and Darwin).
Indian Ocean Dipole: positive IOD (warm western Indian Ocean) can offset El Niño and boost the monsoon (UPSC 2017).
Ocean Mean Temperature (OMT, to 26 °C isotherm depth) predicts monsoon better than SST (UPSC 2020).

nodes.title: Global Climate Change (Causes, impacts, and mitigation strategies)
prelimsNote: Greenhouse gases: CO₂, methane, N₂O, fluorinated gases; water vapour is the most abundant GHG.
Paris Agreement (2015): limit warming well below 2 °C, pursue 1.5 °C; NDCs every 5 years.
India's NDC (2022 update): 45% cut in emissions intensity of GDP by 2030 (vs 2005), 50% non-fossil power capacity by 2030, net zero by 2070.
Impacts: glacier retreat, sea-level rise, coral bleaching, extreme events.

nodes.title: Cyclones — Formation, Classification & India's Vulnerability
prelimsNote: IMD classification by wind speed: depression → cyclonic storm (62–88 km/h) → severe → very severe → extremely severe → super cyclonic (>221 km/h).
Bay of Bengal sees more and stronger cyclones than the Arabian Sea; post-monsoon (Oct–Dec) is the peak season.
Mangroves and coastal shelterbelts reduce storm-surge damage.
Names are drawn from a list prepared by WMO/ESCAP Panel member countries (13 nations, including India).

nodes.title: Ocean Currents — Types, Causes & Climatic Impact
prelimsNote: Causes: planetary winds, temperature and salinity differences (density), Coriolis force, shape of coastline (UPSC 2012).
Warm currents flow from equator poleward along eastern coasts of continents; cold currents along western coasts (Humboldt/Peru, Benguela, California, Canary).
Gulf Stream (warm) keeps NW Europe mild; Kuroshio (warm, Japan); Labrador and Oyashio (cold) — meeting zones form rich fishing grounds (Grand Banks, UPSC 2013).
Sargasso Sea: a sea without coasts in the North Atlantic gyre; equatorial counter-current flows west to east (UPSC 2015).

nodes.title: Coral Reefs — Ecology, Threats & Conservation
prelimsNote: Need warm (20–28 °C), clear, shallow, saline water with sunlight; coral polyps live in symbiosis with zooxanthellae algae.
Types: fringing, barrier (Great Barrier Reef), atolls (Lakshadweep).
Indian reefs: Gulf of Mannar, Gulf of Kachchh, Lakshadweep, Andaman & Nicobar (UPSC 2014).
Bleaching occurs when heat stress expels zooxanthellae; reefs host high biodiversity (UPSC 2018).
Biorock technology restores damaged reefs (UPSC 2022).

nodes.title: Ocean Bottom Relief — Features & Significance
prelimsNote: Continental shelf (shallowest, up to ~200 m, rich in fish and oil), slope, rise, abyssal plain, trenches.
Deepest point: Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench (~11 km); trenches lie at convergent boundaries.
Seamounts (submerged volcanoes) and guyots (flat-topped seamounts); mid-ocean ridges at divergent boundaries.
India's Exclusive Economic Zone extends 200 nautical miles; UNCLOS defines territorial sea (12 nm).

nodes.title: Tides — Causes, Types & Uses
prelimsNote: Caused by gravitational pull of Moon (primary) and Sun, and centrifugal force (UPSC 2015).
Spring tides at new and full moon (Sun–Earth–Moon aligned); neap tides at first and third quarters.
Perigean tides are higher (Moon closest); apogean lower.
Gulf of Khambhat and Gulf of Kachchh have high tidal range suitable for tidal energy.

nodes.title: Ocean Acidification & Marine Ecosystem Degradation
prelimsNote: Oceans absorb ~25–30% of anthropogenic CO₂, forming carbonic acid; pH has fallen ~0.1 since pre-industrial times (UPSC 2011).
Acidification dissolves calcium carbonate shells and coral skeletons.
Dead zones (hypoxia) from nutrient run-off and algal blooms.
Microplastics and microbeads harm marine life (UPSC 2019).

nodes.title: Geopolitical Importance of Indian Ocean
prelimsNote: Only ocean named after a country; chokepoints — Strait of Hormuz, Bab-el-Mandeb, Malacca, Mozambique Channel.
Ten Degree Channel separates Andaman from Nicobar; Nine Degree separates Lakshadweep from Minicoy (UPSC 2014).
Initiatives: IONS (Indian Ocean Naval Symposium, 2008 — UPSC 2017), IORA, SAGAR (Security and Growth for All in the Region).
Chabahar (Iran) gives India access to Afghanistan and Central Asia bypassing Pakistan (UPSC 2017).

nodes.title: Aravalis
prelimsNote: Among the oldest fold mountains in the world (Precambrian, residual); run NE–SW from Delhi to Gujarat.
Highest peak: Guru Shikhar (Mount Abu, ~1,722 m).
Act as a barrier against desert expansion eastwards; Luni river originates near Ajmer.
Trap: the Aravallis are residual/relict fold mountains — not young fold mountains like the Himalaya, and not part of the Vindhya–Satpura system.

nodes.title: Physiography of India
prelimsNote: Six divisions: Himalaya, Northern Plains, Peninsular Plateau, Indian Desert, Coastal Plains, Islands.
Northern Plains: Bhabar (pebbles, streams disappear), Tarai (marshy), Bhangar (old alluvium), Khadar (new alluvium).
Amarkantak is where Vindhya and Satpura meet — not Sahyadri; Biligirirangan hills link Eastern and Western Ghats; Seshachalam is in the Eastern Ghats (UPSC 2023).
Easternmost point: Kibithu (Arunachal); westernmost: Guhar Moti (Gujarat); Indira Point is the southernmost (UPSC 2015, 2017).

nodes.title: Distribution of Rivers & Water Bodies
prelimsNote: Himalayan rivers are perennial (snow-fed), form deltas; peninsular rivers seasonal, mostly east-flowing.
West-flowing rivers through rift valleys: Narmada (between Vindhya and Satpura) and Tapi — form estuaries (UPSC 2013).
Lakes: Wular (largest freshwater; Jhelum passes through it — UPSC 2023), Chilika (largest brackish lagoon), Sambhar (saline), Loktak (phumdis); Kolleru between Godavari and Krishna deltas.
Saline lakes in India: Sambhar, Pangong, Tso Moriri (UPSC 2021).
Groundwater: India is the largest extractor, about a quarter of global withdrawal (UPSC 2023).

nodes.title: Glacier & Ice-Cap Changes — Climate Linkage
prelimsNote: Gangotri (Bhagirathi/Ganga), Yamunotri, Siachen (Nubra), Zemu (Teesta), Bara Shigri (Chenab) — river–glacier pairs (UPSC 2019).
Siachen lies in the Karakoram, the source of the Nubra river (UPSC 2020).
Glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) — South Lhonak (Sikkim, 2023).
Retreating Himalayan glaciers threaten perennial flows of Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra.

nodes.title: Water Body Changes — Lakes, Wetlands & River Systems
prelimsNote: Aral Sea shrank due to Soviet irrigation diversions of Amu Darya and Syr Darya (UPSC 2018); Lake Faguibine (Mali) dried up (UPSC 2022).
Ramsar sites in India exceed 90 (as of 2025); Montreux Record lists threatened Ramsar sites (UPSC 2014).
River-linking: Ken–Betwa first project; Godavari–Krishna link via Polavaram (UPSC 2016).
Saline and brackish lakes: Sambhar, Chilika, Pulicat.

nodes.title: Distribution of Soils — Types & Agricultural Significance
prelimsNote: Alluvial (largest area, rich in potash, poor in nitrogen/phosphorus); khadar (new) vs bhangar (old with kankar).
Black/regur soil: from Deccan basalt, rich in iron, lime, magnesium; high moisture retention, self-ploughing — ideal for cotton (UPSC 2021).
Laterite: leached under high rainfall and temperature, rich in iron/aluminium, poor in humus; good for cashew, tea (UPSC 2013).
Red & yellow soils: iron oxide colour; arid soils: sandy, saline; peaty: Kerala, Sundarbans (humus-rich).
Soil erosion is linked to deforestation, terrace cultivation on steep slopes and tropical climate (UPSC 2014).

nodes.title: Deforestation — Causes, Consequences & Policy Response
prelimsNote: India State of Forest Report (biennial, FSI): forest cover ~21.7%, tree + forest cover ~25% (ISFR 2021/2023).
Largest forest cover by area: Madhya Pradesh; highest % cover: Mizoram (UPSC 2019 tested State forest cover).
Forest Conservation Act 1980 (amended 2023 as Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam); CAMPA funds compensatory afforestation (UPSC 2019).
Green India Mission (NAPCC) aims to increase forest/tree cover (UPSC 2016).

nodes.title: Desertification — Causes, Extent & Mitigation
prelimsNote: UNCCD (1994) is the only legally binding convention on land degradation; India hosted COP14 (2019, Greater Noida).
ISRO's Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas: ~30% of India's land degraded; Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Gujarat most affected.
India's target: restore 26 million ha of degraded land by 2030.
Prosopis juliflora (invasive) spreads in arid lands (UPSC 2018).

nodes.title: Distribution of Minerals — Global & Indian Context
prelimsNote: Iron ore: Odisha, Chhattisgarh (Bailadila), Karnataka, Jharkhand; Bauxite: Odisha, Gujarat; Mica: Andhra, Rajasthan, Jharkhand.
Coal: ~98% Gondwana (Damodar valley); Tertiary coal in Assam/Meghalaya; India imports coking coal for quality reasons (UPSC 2012).
Uranium: Jaduguda (Jharkhand), Tummalapalle (Andhra); monazite (thorium) in Kerala/Tamil Nadu/Odisha beach sands (UPSC 2022).
Cobalt: ~70% of world output from DR Congo (UPSC 2023); ilmenite & rutile are titanium ores (UPSC 2023).
Minor minerals are regulated by State governments (MMDR Act); major minerals by the Centre (UPSC 2018, 2019).

nodes.title: Distribution of Crops — Cropping Patterns Globally & India
prelimsNote: Kharif (sown with monsoon: rice, maize, cotton, jowar, groundnut), Rabi (winter: wheat, mustard, gram), Zaid (summer: watermelon, cucumber).
Rice: high temperature + >100 cm rain (WB, UP, Punjab); wheat: cool growing, warm ripening (UP, Punjab, MP).
Tea: well-drained slopes, frequent rain (Assam, WB, Kerala, Tamil Nadu; also Tripura and Himachal's Kangra valley); coffee in Karnataka.
Jute (WB delta), cotton (black soil — Gujarat, Maharashtra), sugarcane (UP, Maharashtra).
India–China comparison (UPSC 2023): India has more arable land; China higher productivity.

nodes.title: Primary Sector Location Factors — Agriculture, Mining, Fishing
prelimsNote: Agriculture: climate, soil, water, markets, technology — Von Thünen's land-use rings.
Mining is located at the deposit (resource-bound); mineral-rich Chota Nagpur plateau.
Major fishing grounds lie where warm and cold currents meet over continental shelves (UPSC 2013).
India's marine fisheries: west coast more productive (Kerala, Gujarat).

nodes.title: Secondary Sector Location Factors — Manufacturing & Industry
prelimsNote: Weber's least-cost theory: raw material (weight-losing → near source), labour and agglomeration factors.
Iron & steel near coal–iron belts: Jamshedpur, Bhilai, Rourkela, Bokaro, Durgapur; Vizag is a coastal plant.
Cotton textiles: Mumbai, Ahmedabad (market & humid climate); jute: Hooghly belt; sugar shifting to Maharashtra/peninsula.
Footloose industries (electronics) not tied to raw material.
Steel industry pollutants: SOx, NOx, CO, CO₂ (UPSC 2014).

nodes.title: Tertiary Sector Location Factors — Services & Trade
prelimsNote: Services cluster in large cities with skilled labour and connectivity (IT in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune).
India's services exports exceed services imports — services surplus offsets the merchandise deficit (UPSC 2020).
Tourism, trade, transport and communication form the tertiary sector; quaternary = knowledge services.
Special Economic Zones and IT parks promote service exports.

newNodesToCreate.title: Earth Motions, Latitude–Longitude, Time & Eclipses
prelimsNote: On 21 June (summer solstice) the Sun is overhead at the Tropic of Cancer and does not set below the horizon at the Arctic Circle (UPSC 2019).
Longest day in the Northern Hemisphere falls in the second half of June (UPSC 2022); day length varies with latitude due to axial tilt of 23.5° (UPSC 2013).
Earth rotates 15° per hour; IST is based on 82.5°E (Mirzapur); Delhi is at ~77°E longitude (UPSC 2018).
International Date Line (~180°) zig-zags to avoid land; crossing eastward you repeat a day.
Solar eclipse at new moon, lunar eclipse at full moon; umbra gives total, penumbra partial eclipse.

newNodesToCreate.title: Landforms — Weathering, Fluvial, Karst, Glacial, Aeolian & Coastal
prelimsNote: Fluvial: V-shaped valleys, gorges, meanders, ox-bow lakes, deltas; Gandikota canyon is cut by the Pennar (UPSC 2022).
Glacial: U-shaped valleys, cirques, moraines, drumlins; Karst (limestone): sinkholes, stalactites (from roof) and stalagmites (from floor).
Aeolian: barchans, yardangs, mushroom rocks; coastal: cliffs, sea arches, spits, lagoons.
Weathering: physical (frost wedging, exfoliation), chemical (oxidation, carbonation), biological; mass wasting includes landslides.
Ox-bow lakes form from cut-off meanders — Kanwar (Kabar Tal) in Bihar was formed by the meandering Burhi Gandak; UPSC 2023 paired it with Wular (Jhelum) and Kolleru.

newNodesToCreate.title: Ocean Temperature, Salinity & Marine Resources
prelimsNote: Average salinity ~35‰; highest in the Red Sea/Persian Gulf (evaporation), lowest near river mouths and polar seas.
Thermocline: layer of rapid temperature drop; halocline: rapid salinity change.
Upwelling (cold, nutrient-rich water) along western coasts boosts productivity (UPSC 2011).
Polymetallic nodules: India's ISA-licensed area in the Central Indian Ocean Basin; ISA (not a 'Global Ocean Commission') grants seabed licences (UPSC 2021).
Gas hydrates (methane hydrates) found in Krishna–Godavari basin offshore (UPSC 2019).

newNodesToCreate.title: Himalaya, Mountain Passes & Northern Plains
prelimsNote: Himalaya: Trans-Himalaya (Karakoram, Ladakh, Zaskar) → Himadri (Greater) → Himachal (Lesser: Pir Panjal, Dhauladhar) → Shiwaliks (duns like Dehradun).
Passes: Zoji La (Srinagar–Leh), Shipki La (HP–Tibet, Sutlej), Nathu La (Sikkim), Lipulekh (Uttarakhand, Kailash route), Rohtang (Manali–Lahaul); peninsular: Palghat, Bhorghat, Thalghat.
Purvanchal: Patkai, Naga, Mizo hills; Namcha Barwa is the eastern syntaxis.
Peaks: Namcha Barwa is NOT in the Garhwal Himalaya; Nanda Devi is in the Kumaon Himalaya; Nokrek is in Meghalaya, not Sikkim (UPSC 2022).
Himalayan rivers form syntaxial bends and deep gorges; the Himalaya blocks cold Central Asian winds.

newNodesToCreate.title: Peninsular Plateau, Coastal Plains & Island Groups
prelimsNote: Western Ghats (Sahyadri) continuous, higher; Eastern Ghats discontinuous, cut by rivers; they meet in the Nilgiris (Doddabetta).
Coasts: Konkan, Kannada, Malabar (backwaters/kayals) on the west; Coromandel, Northern Circars on the east.
Andaman & Nicobar: Ten Degree Channel separates Little Andaman and Car Nicobar; Great Nicobar is close to Sumatra (UPSC 2014, 2017).
Lakshadweep: coral atolls; Nine Degree Channel separates Minicoy from the rest.
Chandipur (Odisha): sea recedes up to 5 km at low tide (UPSC 2017).

newNodesToCreate.title: Indian Drainage — Himalayan & Peninsular River Systems
prelimsNote: Indus tributaries: Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej (UPSC 2021); Ganga's left-bank: Ramganga, Gomti, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi; right-bank: Yamuna, Son.
Brahmaputra (Tsangpo in Tibet, Siang/Dihang in Arunachal) tributaries: Subansiri, Manas, Teesta, Dibang, Lohit (UPSC 2014, 2016).
Godavari (largest peninsular, 'Dakshin Ganga') tributaries: Pranhita, Indravati, Manjira, Penganga (UPSC 2015).
Krishna: Bhima, Tungabhadra, Ghataprabha, Malaprabha; Cauvery: Kabini, Hemavati — protected areas in the Cauvery basin include Nagarhole and Sathyamangalam (UPSC 2020).
Reservoir–State pairs: Gandhi Sagar (MP), Indira Sagar (MP), Maithon (Jharkhand), Ghataprabha (Karnataka) — UPSC 2022.

newNodesToCreate.title: Natural Vegetation & Forest Types of India
prelimsNote: Tropical evergreen: >200 cm rain (Western Ghats, NE, Andamans); tropical deciduous (monsoon) is the most widespread.
Tropical thorn forests in arid areas; montane forests change with altitude; mangroves in Sundarbans and deltas.
Deciduous trees: teak, sal, mahua; jackfruit is evergreen (UPSC 2023); teak dominates dry deciduous forests (UPSC 2015).
Andaman has tropical rainforests and mangroves (UPSC 2015).
Tropical rainforest soils are nutrient-poor because rapid decomposition and leaching (UPSC 2011, 2023).

newNodesToCreate.title: Transport Network — Ports, Highways, Freight Corridors & Waterways
prelimsNote: Golden Quadrilateral links Delhi–Mumbai–Chennai–Kolkata; East–West corridor runs Silchar–Porbandar, North–South Srinagar–Kanyakumari (UPSC 2023).
Ports: Kamarajar (first corporatised major port), Mundra (largest private), JNPT (largest container port) — UPSC 2023.
DFCs: Eastern (Ludhiana–Sonnagar), Western (Dadri–JNPT).
National Waterways: NW-1 Ganga (Haldia–Prayagraj), NW-2 Brahmaputra (Dhubri–Sadiya), NW-3 West Coast Canal (Kerala).
Trilateral Highway links Moreh (Manipur) with Thailand via Myanmar (UPSC 2023).

newNodesToCreate.title: Population, Census, Urbanisation & Tribes
prelimsNote: Census 2011: population 121 crore, sex ratio 943, child sex ratio 919, literacy 74%, density 382/km²; next census with caste enumeration scheduled for 2027 (as of 2025).
Demographic transition: high birth & death → falling death rate → falling birth rate → low both; India is in stage 3.
Tribes: Gonds (central India), Bhils (W India), Santhals (Jharkhand), Todas (Nilgiris), Chenchus (Andhra), Jarawas & Sentinelese (Andamans); Changpa (Ladakh pastoralists — UPSC 2014).
Living root bridges (Meghalaya, Khasi) and Konyak/Naga traditions are tested as 'tribes & places' (UPSC 2015).

newNodesToCreate.title: World Physical Features — Straits, Seas, Rivers, Mountains & Deserts
prelimsNote: Straits: Malacca (Malaysia–Sumatra), Hormuz (Iran–Oman), Bab-el-Mandeb (Yemen–Djibouti), Bosphorus & Dardanelles (Turkey), Gibraltar, Bering, Dover.
Mediterranean coastal states and Black Sea neighbours are favourite 'how many border' questions (UPSC 2015, 2017, 2019).
Equator passes through Ecuador, Colombia, Brazil, Gabon, Congo, DR Congo, Uganda, Kenya, Somalia, Indonesia, Maldives (UPSC 2011).
Congo Basin covers Cameroon (UPSC 2023); deserts: Atacama (driest, cold Humboldt current), Kalahari, Gobi, Patagonia.
Aral Sea shrank due to irrigation; Dead Sea is the lowest point on land.

newNodesToCreate.title: Places in News — Mapping Geopolitical Flashpoints
prelimsNote: UPSC pairs a region with its country or reason for news — e.g. Donbas (Ukraine), Kachin (Myanmar), Tigray (Ethiopia) — UPSC 2023.
North Kivu & Ituri (DR Congo), Nagorno-Karabakh (Azerbaijan–Armenia), Kherson & Zaporizhzhia (Ukraine) — UPSC 2023 swapped their reasons.
Ukraine's land neighbours: Belarus, Poland, Slovakia, Hungary, Romania, Moldova, Russia (UPSC 2023); Afghanistan's: Iran, Pakistan, China, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan (UPSC 2022).
Levant = eastern Mediterranean shores (UPSC 2022); Senkaku (China–Japan dispute, East China Sea); Sahel coups (Chad, Guinea, Mali, Sudan — UPSC 2023).
Refugee camps: Bidibidi (Uganda, South Sudanese), Dadaab (Kenya, Somalis) — UPSC 2022.

prelimsNote: Map scales: large-scale maps show small areas in detail; projections: Mercator (conformal, distorts area near poles), equal-area, gnomonic.
Boundary lines: Radcliffe (India–Pakistan/Bangladesh), McMahon (India–China, east), Durand (Afghanistan–Pakistan), 38th Parallel (Koreas), 49th Parallel (USA–Canada).
Remote sensing uses (UPSC 2019): crop assessment, groundwater mapping, forest monitoring.
